provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Each input contains solid single-colour rectangles on a background. The output keeps each rectangle's one-cell border and paints everything strictly inside it with colour 8. Hollowing a rectangle looks the same under every rotation and reflection, so the D4 transform needs no direction-specific code. The emitted program works directly in the visible grid coordinates. Only colours are specialised: the background is palette[0] and the fill colour is palette[8], both baked in as constants. The program finds 4-connected single-colour components that are not background. For each one it takes the bounding box and, if the box is at least 3x3, fills the box's interior with the mapped fill colour. This is the same mechanism as the archived solver. The one change is that the background is a fixed constant rather than the most common colour, which stays correct even if the rectangles cover most of the grid.
draft_notes.limitations: Not tested. The program assumes rectangles never touch along an edge. The generator's overlap check with margin 1 implies this. If two same-coloured rectangles did share an edge, they would merge into one component. Rectangles thinner than 3 cells in either direction stay unchanged; the generator never produces them, since its minimum size is 3. I found no conflict between the fixtures and the rule.
